requirements.text: Make this look like a comic book photo

outcomes.description: Transform the image so it has a comic-book visual style while retaining its photographic subject matter.
outcomes.target: The image visibly combines comic-book styling with a photographic appearance.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image, as edited; assess the overall visual treatment for comic-book styling and photographic subject matter.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly have comic-book styling?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comic-book visual styling is visibly present; fail if there is no visible comic-book styling; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Assess the overall visual treatment of the supplied image as edited, without requiring a particular technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image retain recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited image retains recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance; fail if it does not; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient.
nodes.binding: Assess the edited image for photographic subject matter and appearance. This observation describes the result and does not by itself establish progress toward the requested edit.

nodes.question: Compared with the supplied source, does the edited image show a visible change toward a comic-book-photo appearance?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the comparison shows a visible, attributable change toward comic-book visual treatment while remaining recognizably a photo; fail if there is no visible change toward that treatment, including when the edited image merely retains the source appearance; unknown if the comparison or relevant visual evidence is insufficient.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied source and edited images for progress toward the requested comic-book-photo appearance. Do not count unrelated changes or mere retention of the source scene as progress, and do not require a particular technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image fully look like a comic-book photo?
nodes.criteria: Complete if s1 passes and s3 passes. Partial only if s3 passes and evidence establishes the requested appearance remains incomplete. Absent if s3 fails, establishing no requested progress. Unknown if progress or necessary evidence is unresolved. A pass on s2 alone does not establish progress or completion; ignore unrelated edits.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is truncated/ambiguous (“(...)”) and asks whether the image “fully” looks like a comic-book photo, which can blur the distinction between complete fulfillment and any visible progress. Make the target explicit as the requested combination—comic-book visual treatment while retaining photographic subject matter—and keep the node’s outcome tied to the saved progress evidence: completion requires both aspects; partial requires observable comic-book progress that is incomplete; absent requires evidence of no requested progress; unresolved applies when necessary visual evidence is unavailable. Do not treat retained photographic content alone as progress. The repeated valid traces consistently describe the edit as still photographic, with no visible comic-book treatment, supporting absent; the source/edit images likewise show no clear stylistic transformation. Preserve that evidence-based conclusion without turning examples such as outlines or halftones into mandatory criteria. Keep transport failures distinct from visual findings: the one unknown trace is caused by an API/TLS failure, not evidence about the image, so it should remain unresolved rather than count as negative evidence. The high-confidence repeated agreement suggests the main issue is binding clarity and robust handling of unavailable evidence, not a need to force a different label.
s3: Replace the truncated/ambiguous binding with a precise comparison of source and edited images against the requested combined appearance: comic-book visual treatment while retaining recognizable photographic subject matter. Keep this node focused on visible progress, not full completion: distinguish observable but incomplete stylistic progress from no requested progress, and reserve unresolved for unavailable or insufficient visual evidence. Retained photographic content alone is not progress; do not make example techniques such as outlines or halftones mandatory. The supplied images and repeated valid traces show the scene remains photographic without a clear comic-book transformation, supporting no progress; preserve that evidence-based judgment rather than forcing a different label. Keep the API/TLS transport failure separate from visual evidence: it warrants unresolved for that run, not a negative visual finding.
s2: Repair the binding’s truncated/ambiguous target and make this support node assess only the requested comic-book visual treatment, using the source/edit comparison; retaining photographic subject matter is a separate aspect and, by itself, is not evidence of edit progress. Keep the node’s observation distinct from the aggregate fulfillment decision: report visible stylistic progress (including incomplete progress) without requiring any particular technique, and leave completion/partial/no-progress classification to the appropriate downstream logic. The supplied images and repeated high-confidence traces show the same photographic street scene with no clear comic-book transformation, supporting no progress; do not force a different result. Preserve unresolved for unavailable or insufficient image evidence, and keep API/TLS or other execution failures separate from visual findings rather than treating them as negative evidence. The repeated agreement suggests binding clarity and correct evidence routing—not a stricter visual threshold—are the main opportunities.
s1: Repair the truncated/ambiguous binding and keep this support node focused on whether the edit visibly adds comic-book visual treatment, comparing the edited image with the source. Assess visible progress rather than full fulfillment; do not require specific techniques such as outlines or halftones, and do not count unchanged photographic content as progress. The supplied images and repeated high-confidence traces show the street scene remains photographic without a clear comic-book transformation, supporting no visible progress; preserve that evidence-based judgment rather than forcing a different label. Reserve unresolved for insufficient visual evidence, and keep API/TLS or other execution failures separate from visual findings—they are not negative image evidence. Route completion and partial-versus-absent fulfillment to the appropriate downstream logic.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment rule is not faithful to the rubric’s progress semantics. It makes partial depend on s3 passing, although s3 can fail because the comparison shows no requested progress; that is evidence for absent, not partial. Conversely, s3 passing establishes progress but does not establish that the full requested treatment is incomplete, so partial is not justified without evidence of incompleteness. The readout needs to distinguish complete, evidenced progress with incompleteness, no progress, and unresolved evidence. The support checks otherwise cover styling, photographic appearance, and attributable progress without mandating a technique.

The program adds an unsupported requirement: the image must retain photographic subject matter and appearance. The instruction asks for a “comic book photo,” but does not clearly require preserving the original photographic appearance; the program turns that interpretation into a mandatory completion condition. Also, s3 is nested under s2 and only activates after s2 has an observation, yet its progress test must be usable even when photographic appearance is not retained. This structure can leave progress unresolved when s2 is unknown or fails, despite s3 being the separate evidence needed to distinguish progress from no progress. The fulfillment rule otherwise composes the checks consistently, but these issues prevent faithful coverage of the request.
